key_insight: FAMOS shows that articulated object structure can be inferred more reliably by jointly using multiple sparse views instead of relying on a single observation. It predicts both movable-part segmentation and joint parameters in a feed-forward way from partial point clouds.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of modeling articulated objects from sparse monocular observations, where each view only reveals incomplete geometry and limited motion cues. Existing feed-forward methods often depend too much on category-level priors because they reason from just one observation.
method: Takes a sparse, unordered set of partial point clouds as input.
Jointly reasons over multiple observations to recover object articulation.
Predicts movable-part segmentation and joint parameters in a feed-forward framework.
impact: This makes articulated object understanding more practical for robotics, 3D vision, and scene reconstruction under limited-view conditions. For practitioners, it reduces dependence on dense scans or strong prior assumptions while improving robustness to incomplete data.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing multiple sparse point-cloud inputs flowing into a feed-forward model.
Side-by-side visualization of partial observations versus predicted articulated parts and joints.
Color-coded segmentation overlay on a 3D object to highlight movable parts.
Icon-based comparison of single-view prior-heavy methods vs multi-view joint reasoning.
paper_title: FAMOS: Feed-Forward 3D Articulation Modeling from Sparse Observations
paper_authors: Kevin Qu, Tao Sun, Massimiliano Viola, Liyuan Zhu, Zhizhuo Zhou
